Abstract.AbstractText: Herein, we present a first report on the luminescence thermometry properties of Er, Yb doped Gd2O2S microparticles under near infrared up-conversion excitation around 980 and 1500 nm measured in the 280 to 800 K interval. The thermometry properties are assessed using both cw and ns pulsed excitation as well as tuning the excitation wavelength across Yb and Er absorption profiles. For low cw (300 mW/cm-1) as well as pulsed ns (400 ÷ 550 mW/cm-1) excitation modes, no thermal load is observed. The maximum relative sensitivity values are ~0.01 and ~0.008 % K-1 for ns pulsed excitation at 980 and 1500 nm, respectively at the room-temperature of 280 K. Our findings evidence interesting up-conversion and thermometry properties Er doped Gd2O2S under near-infrared excitation and highlight the need to explore further these properties in the nanoparticulate regime.
